A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HYPER paper, with all 34 pages and Appendices A-G available. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2-34 are identical; page 1 differs only in an author affiliation and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original HYPER experiments on inductive hypergraph link prediction, including benchmark results in Tables 2-3, ablations, and additional knowledge-graph and scalability experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original benchmark, ablation, knowledge-graph, and scalability results, including the detailed experimental tables in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G.4-G.5 retain identical relation and entity encoders, positional-interaction encoding, message-passing procedures, decoder, and training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 16 constructed hypergraph benchmarks, three existing node-inductive hypergraph benchmarks, knowledge-graph evaluations in Appendix E, and pretraining corpora in Table 13.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments, including G-MPNN and HCNet in Table 2, the additional node-inductive baselines in Table 3, ULTRA variants, and KG-ICL variants in Table 12.

E3.justification: Dataset construction and splits, filtered ranking, metrics, reification procedures, model configurations, and training schedules are unchanged in Section 5.1, Appendices A and G, and Tables 22-23.

E4.justification: Both retain identical pretraining-mixture comparisons, positional-encoder ablations, argument-position corruption experiments, scalability analyses, and alternative-reification comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices F and G.3.

E5.justification: Both state that experimental results are averaged over three runs and retain identical standard-deviation reporting in Tables 19-21. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are identical, including Tables 2-4, Figure 6, and appendix Tables 8-12 and 19-21. For example, zero-shot HYPER(3KG+2HG) MRR on JF-25 remains 0.216 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 4.1, invariance and positional-encoder proofs in Appendix C, and complexity derivations in Appendix F.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion make identical claims about generalization to unseen entities and relations of arbitrary arity and performance against existing methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including explanations of reification and pretraining effects, quadratic growth of positional interactions with arity, and the acknowledged performance gap on standard knowledge graphs.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware, training-time, hyperparameter, and schedule disclosures in Appendices B, D, and G are identical. The stated code-access information also remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and comparisons with prior work are identical. No cited works or research-positioning statements are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Page 1 adds University of Oxford to İsmail İlkan Ceylan's TU Wien & AITHYRA affiliation. The arXiv stamp changes from v2, 13 February 2026 to v3, 8 May 2026. Scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-7, Tables 1-23, captions, formatting, and placement are unchanged. The longer affiliation remains on the same line without reflowing the page; pages 2-34 render identically.

improvement.justification: The only differences are an affiliation addition and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, so these administrative updates do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
